name: Romestecq
summary: Historical Dutch trick-taking card game for two teams with melds and chalk scoring.
rules_text: Use a 36-card French pack, Ace high to Six low. Play is 2, 4 or 6 in two equal teams; with six the middle player of each trio cuts, high card chooses dealer and opposing middle scores. Dealer deals 5 cards each, in any packet size, but the same dealing pattern must be kept for the whole partie. Before first trick players check melds: Virlique (four of a kind) wins immediately, higher rank beats lower; Triche (three of a kind) 3 pts if Aces/Kings else 2; Double Ningre (two Aces+two Kings etc) 3; Village (two Queen/Jack pairs of same suits) 2; Rome (pair below King) 1; Double Rome (Ace or King pair) 2. Melds are announced when the first card of the meld is played to a trick. No trumps, must follow suit if able. Highest of led suit wins trick and leads next. Winning last trick scores 1 for Stecq. First team to 21 points, or 36 with six players, wins.
rating_reason: Team trick-taking, variable players, specific historic game.
